newsitem.title: INDIA: Paribas puts sell on India's SAIL.
newsitem.headline: Paribas puts sell on India's SAIL.

text.p: Securities firm Paribas Asia Equity said on Wednesday it had downgraded its recommendation on shares of Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) to "sell" from "no action."
SAIL is India's leading state-owned steel maker.

"This follows our downgrading of the company's EPS forecast for 1997/98 which makes the company appear quite expensive relative to both the sector and the Indian market," Paribas' Asian steel analyst Rajeev R. Das said in a July 28 report.

"We are cutting our 1997/98 earnings estimate by 13 percent to 1.42 rupees. This values the SAIL local shares at more than 16 times FY1998 projected earnings - or at a small 10 percent discount to the Indian market," the report said.
"If we remove the MNC (multinational companies) stocks that trade at high PERs (price earning ratios) from the market, then the SAIL stock is trading at 25 percent premium to the market."
Given the bleak outlook the company faces and the relatively flat earnings projected for this year, this premium valuation is unjustified, Paribas Asia Equity said.
Paribas said it expected SAIL to book huge depreciation and interest charges related to the Durgapur steel plant modernisation this year.
It said recent price hikes by Indian steel firms had come at an opportune time for SAIL, helping it to reduce the discounts it had started offering customers.

Rather than getting a price hike, most Indian steel makers have lowered their price discounts. "While there may be a brief firmness in Indian prices, we expect new capacities by the year end to soften prices again," the report said.
"There seems to be some mistaken notion that SAIL will somehow benefit from the rising steel prices," Das told Reuters. "But we think SAIL will miss out on this brief upturn in the steel cycle."
